mn62:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
mn62:2.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms.
mn62:2.2: Also venerable Rāhula, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, followed along close behind the Fortunate One.
mn62:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, looking back, addressed venerable Rāhula, saying:
mn62:3.2: “Whatever form there is, Rāhula, past, future, or present, inside or outside, gross or subtle, base or excellent, whether far or near, (in regard to) all form: “This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self,” like this it ought to be seen as it really is, with right wisdom.”
mn62:3.3: “Only form, Fortunate One? Only form, Happy One?”
mn62:3.4: “Form, Rāhula - and feelings, Rāhula - and perceptions, Rāhula - and (mental) processes, Rāhula - and consciousness, Rāhula.”
mn62:4.1: Then venerable Rāhula thought: “Who today, when the Fortunate One has advised him with (such) advice to his face, could enter a village for alms?” Therefore having turned back he sat down at the root of a certain tree. After folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight, he established mindfulness at the front.
mn62:5.1: Venerable Sāriputta saw that venerable Rāhula was sitting down at the root of a certain tree, and had folded his legs crosswise, set his body straight, and established mindfulness at the front,
mn62:5.2: and having seen him, he addressed venerable Rāhula, saying:
mn62:5.3: “Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is mindfulness while breathing.
mn62:5.4: Mindfulness while breathing, Rāhula, when it has been developed and made much of yields great fruit and brings great advantages.”
mn62:6.1: Then venerable Rāhula rising from seclusion in the evening time approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side, venerable Rāhula said this to the Fortunate One:
mn62:7.1: “How, reverend Sir, does mindfulness while breathing when it has been developed and made much of yield great fruit, bring great advantages?”
mn62:8.1: “Whatever there is, Rāhula, that is inside, in oneself, that is hard or has become solid, and is attached to, like this:
mn62:8.2: head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone-marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, excrement - or whatever else there is that is inside, in oneself, that is hard, or has become solid, and is attached to,
mn62:8.3: that, Rāhula, is called the internal earth element.
mn62:8.4: Now, that which is the internal earth element, and that which is the external earth element, that is only the earth element.
mn62:8.5: “This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self,” like this it ought to be seen, as it really is, with right wisdom.
mn62:8.6: Having seen it like this, as it really is, with right wisdom, one loses interest in the earth element, one detaches the mind from the earth element.
mn62:9.1: And what, Rāhula, is the water-element?
mn62:9.2: The water element may be internal or may be external.
mn62:9.3: And what, Rāhula, is the internal water element?
mn62:9.4: That which is inside, in oneself, that is water, or has become watery, and is attached to, like this:
mn62:9.5: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, oil, tears, grease, spit, mucus, synovial fluid, urine - or whatever else there is that is inside, in oneself, that is water, or has become watery, and is attached to,
mn62:9.6: that, Rāhula, is called the internal water element.
mn62:9.7: Now, that which is the internal water element, and that which is the external water element, that is only the water element.
mn62:9.8: “This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self,” like this it ought to be seen, as it really is, with right wisdom.
mn62:9.9: Having seen it like this, as it really is, with right wisdom, one loses interest in the water element, one detaches the mind from the water element.
mn62:10.1: And what, Rāhula, is the fire element?
mn62:10.2: The fire element may be internal or may be external.
mn62:10.3: And what, Rāhula, is the internal fire element?
mn62:10.4: That which is inside, in oneself, that is fire, or has become fiery, and is attached to, like this:
mn62:10.5: that by which one is heated, by which one grows old, by which one is burned up, by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, gets completely digested - or whatever else there is that is inside, in oneself, that is fire, or has become fiery, and is attached to,
mn62:10.6: that, Rāhula, is called the internal fire element.
mn62:10.7: Now, that which is the internal fire element, and that which is the external fire element, that is only the fire element.
mn62:10.8: “This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self,” like this it ought to be seen, as it really is, with right wisdom.
mn62:10.9: Having seen it like this, as it really is, with right wisdom, one loses interest in the fire element, one detaches the mind from the fire element.
mn62:11.1: And what, Rāhula, is the wind element?
mn62:11.2: The wind element may be internal or may be external.
mn62:11.3: And what, Rāhula, is the internal wind element?
mn62:11.4: That which is inside, in oneself, that is wind, or has become windy, and is attached to, like this:
mn62:11.5: winds that go up, winds that go down, winds in the bowels, winds in the belly, winds that go through the limbs, in-breath, out-breath - or whatever else there is that is inside, in oneself, that is wind, or has become windy, and is attached to,
mn62:11.6: that, Rāhula, is called the internal wind element.
mn62:11.7: Now, that which is the internal wind element, and that which is the external wind element, that is only the wind element.
mn62:11.8: “This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self,” like this it ought to be seen, as it really is, with right wisdom.
mn62:11.9: Having seen it like this, as it really is, with right wisdom, one loses interest in the wind element, one detaches the mind from the wind element.
mn62:12.1: And what, Rāhula, is the space element?
mn62:12.2: The space element may be internal or may be external.
mn62:12.3: And what, Rāhula, is the internal space element?
mn62:12.4: That which is inside that is space, or has become spacy, and is attached to, like this:
mn62:12.5: ear-holes, nose-holes, the door of the mouth, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is swallowed, that place where what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted settles, and the lower part by which that which is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted goes out - or whatever else there is that is inside, in oneself, that is space, or has become spacy, and is attached to,
mn62:12.6: that, Rāhula, is called the internal space element.
mn62:12.7: Now, that which is the internal space element, and that which is the external space element, that is only the space element.
mn62:12.8: “This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self,” like this it ought to be seen, as it really is, with right wisdom.
mn62:12.9: Having seen it like this, as it really is, with right wisdom, one loses interest in the space element, one detaches the mind from the space element.
mn62:13.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is to be even as the earth,
mn62:13.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as the earth, appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:13.3: Just as, Rāhula, they throw what is clean on the earth, and they throw what is unclean, and they throw what has become dung, and they throw what has become urine, and they throw what has become spit, and they throw what has become pus, and they throw what has become blood, but the earth is not distressed, or ashamed, or disgusted by it,
mn62:13.4: just so do you, Rāhula, develop the meditation that is to be even as the earth,
mn62:13.5: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as the earth appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:14.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is to be even as water,
mn62:14.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as water, appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:14.3: Just as, Rāhula, they wash away what is clean in the water, and they wash away what is unclean, and they wash away what has become dung, and they wash away what has become urine, and they wash away what has become spit, and they wash away what has become pus, and they wash away what has become blood, but the water is not distressed, or ashamed, or disgusted by it,
mn62:14.4: just so do you, Rāhula, develop the meditation that is to be even as water,
mn62:14.5: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as water appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:15.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is to be even as fire,
mn62:15.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as fire, appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:15.3: Just as, Rāhula, fire burns what is clean, and fire burns what is unclean, and fire burns what has become dung, and fire burns what has become urine, and fire burns what has become spit, and fire burns what has become pus, and fire burns what has become blood, but the fire is not distressed, or ashamed, or disgusted by it,
mn62:15.4: just so do you, Rāhula, develop the meditation that is to be even as fire,
mn62:15.5: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as fire appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:16.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is to be even as the wind,
mn62:16.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as the wind, appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:16.3: Just as, Rāhula, the wind blows over what is clean, and it blows over what is unclean, and it blows over what has become dung, and it blows over what has become urine, and it blows over what has become spit, and it blows over what has become pus, and it blows over what has become blood, but the wind is not distressed, or ashamed, or disgusted by it,
mn62:16.4: just so do you, Rāhula, develop the meditation that is to be even as the wind,
mn62:16.5: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as the wind appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:17.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is to be even as space,
mn62:17.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as space, appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:17.3: Just as, Rāhula, space doesn't settle anywhere,
mn62:17.4: just so do you, Rāhula, develop the meditation that is to be even as space,
mn62:17.5: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is to be even as space, appealing and unappealing contacts that have arisen in the mind will not take a hold there.
mn62:18.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is friendliness,
mn62:18.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is friendliness whatever ill-will there is will be given up.
mn62:19.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is kindness,
mn62:19.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is kindness whatever violence there is will be given up.
mn62:20.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is gladness,
mn62:20.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is gladness whatever discontent there is will be given up.
mn62:21.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is equanimity,
mn62:21.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is equanimity whatever resentment there is will be given up.
mn62:22.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, on the unattractive,
mn62:22.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation on the unattractive whatever passion there is will be given up.
mn62:23.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is the perception of impermanence,
mn62:23.2: for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is the perception of impermanence whatever (kind of) ‘I am’ conceit there is will be given up.
mn62:24.1: Develop the meditation, Rāhula, that is mindfulness while breathing,
mn62:24.2: mindfulness while breathing, Rāhula, when developed and made much of yields great fruit, brings great advantages.
mn62:24.3: And how, Rāhula, does mindfulness while breathing when it has been developed and made much of yield great fruit and bring great advantages?
mn62:25.1: Here, Rāhula, a monk who has gone to the wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty place, sits down. After folding his legs crosswise, setting his body straight, and establishing mindfulness at the front,
mn62:25.2: ever mindful he breathes in, mindful he breathes out.
mn62:26.1: While breathing in long, he knows “I am breathing in long”, while breathing out long, he knows “I am breathing out long”,
mn62:26.2: while breathing in short, he knows “I am breathing in short”, while breathing out short, he knows “I am breathing out short”,
mn62:26.3: he trains like this: experiencing the whole body I will breathe in, he trains like this: experiencing the whole body I will breathe out,
mn62:26.4: he trains like this: making the bodily process calm I will breathe in, he trains like this: making the bodily process calm I will breathe out.
mn62:27.1: He trains like this: experiencing joy I will breathe in, he trains like this: experiencing joy I will breathe out,
mn62:27.2: he trains like this: experiencing pleasure I will breathe in, he trains like this: experiencing pleasure I will breathe out,
mn62:27.3: he trains like this: experiencing the mental process I will breathe in, he trains like this: experiencing the mental process I will breathe out,
mn62:27.4: he trains like this: making the mental process calm I will breathe in, he trains like this: making the mental process calm I will breathe out.
mn62:28.1: He trains like this: experiencing the mind I will breathe in, he trains like this: experiencing the mind I will breathe out,
mn62:28.2: he trains like this: gladdening the mind I will breathe in, he trains like this: gladdening the mind I will breathe out,
mn62:28.3: he trains like this: concentrating the mind I will breathe in, he trains like this: concentrating the mind I will breathe out,
mn62:28.4: he trains like this: freeing the mind I will breathe in, he trains like this: freeing the mind I will breathe out.
mn62:29.1: He trains like this: contemplating impermanence I will breathe in, he trains like this: contemplating impermanence I will breathe out,
mn62:29.2: he trains like this: contemplating dispassion I will breathe in, he trains like this: contemplating dispassion I will breathe out,
mn62:29.3: he trains like this: contemplating cessation I will breathe in, he trains like this: contemplating cessation I will breathe out,
mn62:29.4: he trains like this: contemplating letting go I will breathe in, he trains like this: contemplating letting go I will breathe out.
mn62:30.1: In this way, Rāhula, mindfulness while breathing when it has been developed like this and made much of yields great fruit, brings great advantages.
mn62:30.2: In this way, Rāhula, through the development of mindfulness while breathing, through making much of it, the in-breaths and the out-breaths at the end are understood as they cease, they are surely understood.”
mn62:30.4: and venerable Rāhula was uplifted and greatly rejoiced in what was said by the Fortunate One.
